title: What does DIDDelete do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of DIDDelete and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, DIDDelete removes the account's decentralized-identifier entry from the XRPL. [1]

The owner deletes its DID object rather than deleting the account or its transaction history. External documents referenced by the identifier can still exist elsewhere. Resolve current ledger state before treating a historical identifier as active. A deletion record can establish lifecycle status without establishing who controlled every earlier off-ledger representation. [1]

The DIDDelete reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using DIDDelete, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
